criteria.span: Stable with ≤ 20 mg prednisone (or equivalent) qd

criteria.text: Cardiologist approval if unstable angina, LVEF not estimable, non-sinus rhythm, PVCs, etc.
criteria.span: Approval for surgery by cardiologist if any of the following are present

criteria.text: Post-rehabilitation approval by pulmonary physician, thoracic surgeon, and anesthesiologist
criteria.span: Approval for surgery by pulmonary physician, thoracic surgeon, and anesthesiologist post-rehabilitation

criteria.text: Plasma cotinine <= 13.7 ng/mL (or carboxyhemoglobin <= 2.5% if using nicotine products)
criteria.span: Plasma cotinine level ≤13.7 ng/mL (or arterial carboxyhemoglobin ≤ 2.5% if using nicotine products)

criteria.text: Nonsmoking for 4 months before the initial interview and throughout evaluation
criteria.span: Nonsmoking for 4 months prior to initial interview and throughout evaluation for surgery

criteria.text: Severe upper-lobe-predominant emphysema, or severe non-upper-lobe emphysema with low exercise capacity (<= 25 W women, <= 40 W men)
criteria.span: Patients with low exercise capacity are those whose maximal exercise capacity is at or below 25 watts for women and 40 watts (w) for men

criteria.text: Excluded: non-upper-lobe emphysema with high exercise capacity (> 25 W women, > 40 W men)
criteria.span: has severe, non-upper lobe emphysema with high exercise capacity

criteria.text: Excluded: FEV1 <= 20% predicted with homogeneous emphysema or DLCO <= 20% predicted
criteria.span: The patient presents with FEV1 ≤ 20% of predicted value, and either homogeneous distribution of emphysema on CT scan, or carbon monoxide diffusing capacity of ≤ 20% of predicted value

criteria.text: Facility: Joint Commission LVRS Disease Specific Care certified, or Medicare-approved lung/heart-lung transplant hospital
criteria.span: certified by the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (Joint Commission) under the LVRS Disease Specific Care Certification Program

criteria.text: Preoperative program: 16-20 sessions over 6-10 weeks, each >= 2 hours
criteria.span: The program must include a 6- to 10-week series of at least 16, and no more than 20, preoperative sessions, each lasting a minimum of 2 hours.

criteria.text: Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation
criteria.span: Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation

cases.note: All criteria met; upper-lobe-predominant disease, so exercise capacity (45 W) does not matter.
cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 26.4 kg/m2. He has been stable for 6 months on prednisone 5 mg daily. HRCT shows bilateral emphysema that the radiologist reads as severe and upper lobe predominant. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 60%; he is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions on resting EKG and no angina. He completed an 8-week preoperative program of 18 sessions of 2.5 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 7 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 265 m and he completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program was 45 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. He quit smoking 3 years ago; plasma cotinine is 3 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is planned at a hospital approved by Medicare as a lung transplantation hospital.
